solution.p: From the graph, we see that f(x) appears to have one critical point, at x=0, and two inflection points, one between 0 and 1 and the other between 0 and -1.
To find the critical points, we set f'(x) = 0. Since f'(x) = 3(-2(9)x) e^{-9 x^2} = 0, there is one solution, x = 0. The only critical point is at x=0.

To find the inflection points, we find f''(x) and determine where it is zero. f''(x) = 3( -2(9) e^{-9 x^2} + 4(9)^2 x^2 e^{-9 x^2} = 54 e^{-9 x^2} ( -1 + 18 x^2 ). For this to be zero, we must have -1 + 18 x^2 = 0, or x = \pm 1/\sqrt{18}. There are exactly two inflection points, at x = -1/\sqrt{18} \approx -0.236 and x = 1/\sqrt{18} \approx 0.236.
